arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: The creditor's lawyer argued good faith belief blocks contempt liability.
The debtor's lawyer argued good faith does not excuse ignoring orders.
Justice Alito questioned if a good faith belief prevents a violation.
Justice Sotomayor asked if debtors must use safe harbors to avoid liability.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests whether a creditor's honest belief excuses a bankruptcy violation. The lower court found a violation despite that belief. The Supreme Court must decide if good faith blocks liability.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This dispute defines the limits of creditor power. It determines whether honest mistakes excuse legal violations. It shapes how courts enforce bankruptcy orders. It affects the balance between debtor rights and creditor interests.
